description: We are NoSleepClub, we focus on machine-learning/data-related challenges and hackathons. Our core team consists of three members who specialize on data science, algorithms, artificial intelligence, web developments and applying our skills to solve real problems.
summary: Touch The Sky is a bilingual learning website for middle-school students and anyone curious about space. It combines Sphere X Learn, a 3D spaceship game, with an interactive SPHEREx guide and a browser-based sky explorer. Players study visual lessons, answer questions with Alien X, and earn fuel to advance the ship’s story. The lessons introduce infrared light, filter bands, spectra, water-ice signatures in star-forming regions, and basic methods for checking and comparing astronomical images. The mission guide explains SPHEREx’s science goals, spacecraft and instruments. Explore the Sky lets users search by celestial coordinates and inspect SPHEREx observations from NASA/IPAC IRSA. The project teaches both the science behind the mission and the tools used to explore its data, while explaining that image differences alone do not confirm a discovery.
details:
Touch The Sky is a bilingual learning site for middle-school students and space enthusiasts. Sphere X Learn is a 3D spaceship game: learners explore the ship with Gagoo, study a lesson on the tablet, meet Alien X for a six-question quiz, and earn fuel to advance through the game’s fictional flight. A separate learning library offers three short lessons with activities and quizzes.

The lessons ask why SPHEREx revisits a sky field, how to follow sources across images, and whether a bright pixel has really disappeared. Interactive activities introduce infrared light, filter bands, false-color images, spectra and water-ice signatures in Cygnus X. Learners also practice checking dates and wavelengths, reading missing-data and quality flags, and aligning images using nearby stars. The mission guide explains the spacecraft, six detectors and 102 spectral channels across 0.75–5.0 µm, linking them to the science goals: galaxy clustering and cosmic inflation, the combined infrared glow of galaxies, and interstellar ice.

Explore the Sky queries NASA/IPAC IRSA. Users select one of five targets or enter RA/Dec, choose a 3.6–24 arcmin field of view, DR1 or QR3, a detector band and optional dates. The app retrieves observations and FITS cutouts, uses WCS/SIP metadata to align frames on a shared sky grid, and supports A/B comparisons and playback of compatible observations. Frames show UTC dates, observation IDs, wavelengths, quality flags, missing pixels and source links. A saved three-image Epsilon Indi B sequence provides an example. Image differences alone do not establish motion or variability. Game fuel, characters and flight effects are fictional, not SPHEREx telemetry.

The site uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js and Python tools including Astropy, NumPy and Pillow. OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted with research, coding and editing; no AI/ML model is embedded in the site.
